---
title: "Median contract rent and the five-year violent crime rate in Chicago"
output: html_document
params:
  model_data: ""
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
w <- jsonlite::read_json(params$model_data, simplifyVector=TRUE)
stopifnot(w$version == 4L)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f%%", x)
interval <- function(lo, hi) paste(pct(lo), "to", pct(hi))
```

## Study design

The four models use the same `r format(w$sample_n, big.mark=",")` block groups and
give each area equal weight. The outcome is log median monthly contract rent.
The exposure is the number of geocoded CPD violent crimes in 2020–2024 divided by
the block group's ACS five-year total population estimate, multiplied by 1,000.
Each retained block group has a positive population, usable rent and controls,
and at least half its polygon area inside Chicago.

## Staged results

The rent differences below correspond to `r round(w$crime_contrast,1)` more
recorded violent crimes per 1,000 residents over five years, the observed
interquartile range. Intervals use HC3 standard errors.

```{r stages, echo=FALSE}
m <- w$models
e <- w$effects[match(m$model,w$effects$model),]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model=m$model, Specification=m$specification,
  R2=pct(100*m$r_squared), Rent_difference=pct(e$percent_estimate),
  HC3_interval=interval(e$percent_hc3_conf_low,e$percent_hc3_conf_high)),
  col.names=c("Model","Specification","R²","Rent difference","95% interval"))
```

M4 compares areas within the same community, adjusting for housing, renter and
socioeconomic characteristics. Its confidence interval includes zero. These
area-level associations cannot establish what a change in crime would do to rent.

## Period and weighting checks

The same crime-rate difference is used in every row. Each period uses its own
block-group boundaries, complete cases and ACS population denominators.

```{r robustness, echo=FALSE}
p <- w$period_checks
knitr::kable(data.frame(Period=paste(p$year-4,p$year,sep="–"), Weight=p$weighting,
  Areas=p$n, Rent_difference=pct(p$contrast_pct_estimate),
  CI=interval(p$contrast_pct_hc3_conf_low,p$contrast_pct_hc3_conf_high)),
  col.names=c("ACS period","Block-group weight","Block groups","M4 rent difference","95% interval"))
```

## Measurement and coverage

Population is ACS cell B03002_001. The rate uses recorded homicide, criminal sexual
assault, robbery and aggravated assault/battery with usable locations.
Incidents may involve visitors, and recording and geographic coverage vary.
Regression intervals treat the population denominator as fixed. Differences
across periods may also reflect which areas had publishable rent and income.

## Fit and diagnostics

```{r validation, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model=m$model, Fit=pct(100*m$adjusted_r_squared),
  Held_out=pct(100*m$predictive_R2), RMSE=round(m$RMSE_log,3)),
  col.names=c("Model","Adjusted R²","Held-out R²","Held-out RMSE (log rent)"))
```

Cross-validation uses tract-based folds. The community-area model requires a
community observed in the training fold, so all stages use the same held-out
areas. The primary fits give each block group equal weight. The following
sensitivity fits use the same four stages under narrower sample definitions.

```{r sample-checks, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Sample=w$sensitivity$sensitivity, Areas=w$sensitivity$n,
                        M4=pct(100*w$sensitivity$M4)),
             col.names=c("Sample","Block groups","M4 R²"))
```

## Final model coefficients

The crime coefficient below is per one additional recorded crime per 1,000
residents over five years. Housing and demographic shares are per ten percentage
points. Income enters as log median household income. Intervals are in log-rent
units. A community with one retained area has no estimable HC3 interval for its
indicator.

```{r coefficients, echo=FALSE}
co <- subset(w$formal_coefficients, model == "M4")
knitr::kable(co[c("label","estimate","hc3_conf_low","hc3_conf_high")], digits=5,
  col.names=c("Term","Coefficient","95% HC3 lower","95% HC3 upper"))
```
